title: Prepare and hold a mare for service

lessons.title: Preparing the mare and the breeding area
lessons.html:
Before the covering

In-hand breeding is one of the most dangerous jobs on a stud farm. A stallion can weigh over 500 kg and a mare that is not fully ready may kick hard. Careful preparation protects the mare, the stallion and the handlers.

Confirm the mare is ready

  • The mare should have been teased and show strong signs of oestrus: leaning towards the teaser, lifting the tail, squatting, urinating and "winking" the vulva.
  • The stud vet often scans the mare to time ovulation and confirm she is ready to be covered.
  • Check the breeding records: correct mare, correct stallion as booked, and any veterinary swab results required by the stud or breed society.

Prepare the breeding shed or area

  • Non-slip, soft footing such as rubber, sand or sawdust. No hard concrete.
  • Enough space, high roof, no protruding objects, and clear exits for handlers.
  • Good light and quiet surroundings.
  • Equipment ready: halters and lead shanks, kicking boots (felt boots for the mare's hind feet), tail bandage, buckets of clean warm water, disposable gloves, cotton wool, twitch if the stud's policy allows it.

Prepare the mare

  1. Put on a well-fitted halter or bridle with a lead shank.
  2. Bandage the tail from the top to below the vulva so hair does not cut the stallion or carry dirt into the mare.
  3. Wash the vulva and surrounding area with clean warm water and cotton wool, from the centre outwards, using fresh cotton each time. Rinse well and dry. Do not use strong soaps or disinfectants unless the vet has prescribed them, because they can harm sperm.
  4. Fit kicking boots on the hind feet, or remove the hind shoes, according to stud procedure.
  5. If the mare has a foal at foot, keep the foal safely in a stall or pen where the mare can see it, to keep her calm.

lessons.title: Holding the mare during service
lessons.html:
The mare handler's position

The mare handler stands at the mare's near (left) side, at her head and shoulder, facing slightly towards her. Hold the lead shank in folds, never wrapped around the hand. Wear a helmet, gloves and sturdy boots. Never stand directly in front of the mare, because she may jump forward.

Restraint aids

  • Kicking boots on the hind feet soften a kick.
  • Twitch: applied to the upper lip, used briefly where the stud policy and the vet allow it; it releases calming substances when correctly applied.
  • Holding up a foreleg: some studs have a second handler lift a foreleg until the stallion mounts, then release it so the mare can balance.
  • Breeding hobbles or a breeding stock on some studs.

During the covering

  1. Position the mare against a padded wall or in the open as the stud prefers, standing square.
  2. The stallion handler brings the stallion from the near side at an angle, never straight from behind, and allows him to tease her briefly.
  3. Keep the mare's head straight and still with gentle but firm contact. Speak calmly.
  4. When the stallion mounts, step back slightly to the side, still controlling the head, and keep the mare from swinging her hindquarters away.
  5. Watch the stallion's tail flagging, which shows ejaculation. The stallion handler will then back him away.
  6. As the stallion dismounts, turn the mare's head towards the stallion so her hindquarters swing away from him. This protects the stallion and handlers from a kick.

After service

  • Walk the mare quietly for a few minutes.
  • Remove boots and tail bandage, check her for injuries.
  • Record date, time, stallion and any problems in the breeding register.
  • Return her to her foal or paddock.

Key points

  • Confirm oestrus and the booking before preparing the mare.
  • Use a safe area with non-slip footing and clear exits.
  • Bandage the tail and wash the vulva with clean warm water only.
  • Hold the mare at the near side shoulder, rope in folds, wearing a helmet.
  • Turn the mare's head towards the stallion as he dismounts.
  • Record every service in the breeding register.

quiz.question: Which is a strong sign that a mare is in oestrus?

options.text: Pinning her ears at the teaser
Lifting the tail and winking the vulva

quiz.question: Why is the mare's tail bandaged before service?

options.text: So hair does not cut the stallion or carry dirt

quiz.question: What should be used to wash the mare's vulva?

options.text: Clean warm water and cotton wool

quiz.question: Where does the mare handler stand?

options.text: Directly in front of the mare
At the near side, at her head and shoulder

quiz.question: As the stallion dismounts, which way should the mare's head be turned?

options.text: Towards the stallion so her hindquarters swing away
